correctness.rationale: For every integer n>=5, the graph J(n,2) has N=binom(n,2) vertices and unit edge conductances. Its incidence matrix B yields Laplacian 2(n−1)I−BᵀB and two nonzero spectral values n and 2(n−1). Two incidence dipoles have only the five orbit invariants (k,h)=(1,1),(1,0),(0,2),(0,1),(0,0), which give mixed L+ and (L+)² entries c_{k,h} and t_{k,h}. The diagonal r=(n+1)/(n(n−1)) is <1 and the 2×2 Woodbury denominator (1−r)²−c² is positive for n>=5, so any two-edge deletion remains connected and its Kirchhoff increase is the stated rational F_n(k,h). Orbit counting gives all five nonzero multiplicities, whose total is binom(|E|,2); symbolic positive rational differences establish strictly I_triangle>I_nontriangle>D2>D1>D0 and the displayed global maximum. Fresh independent enumeration exhausted every pair of edges for J(5,2) (435 pairs) and J(6,2) (1770 pairs), confirmed classes/multiplicities, and directly recomputed five representative Kirchhoff differences using grounded-Laplacian matrix inversion. General theorem rests on symbolic spectral proof, not finite cases.

originality.rationale: The five simultaneous two-edge-failure motif values and strict universal ordering for J(n,2), n>=5, are not provided by inspected general pseudoinverse, network robustness, edge-flow-redistribution or graph-spectral references. T(4) is a complete multipartite covered special case and is deliberately excluded. The method is classical but the full orbit-resolved failure classification is assessed as new to best knowledge.

value.rationale: When a network uses pairwise interactions modeled by the triangular graph, all single failures are symmetric, so the exact double-failure damage classes distinguish its first nontrivial reliability behavior. A sharp maximizer shape, all class multiplicities and exact objective values are natural graph-resistance invariants of an infinite graph family, useful beyond a routine spectral exercise.
